answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake: every agent locks a bond that is slashed when fraud is proven, so spinning up fake identities costs real money instead of being free. Reputation then grows only from verified work over time — an agent at the zenith of trust has a long checkable history, while new accounts begin in the saffron-lit foothills with limited rights. At each summit review, randomly chosen peers re-audit contributions, exposing clusters of sock-puppets that share funding or behavior, which makes large-scale fakery uneconomic.
